transcript.text: Alright everyone, thanks for being here. We've got 30 kilograms of apples from the backyard orchard to sort this weekend into three categories: family use, community pantry donation, and freezer storage. Before I make the final call on the split and preparation, let's go around the table like we usually do so each of you can mention any practical details that should shape the plan. Who'd like to start?
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: I spoke with Grandma yesterday, and she specifically asked for exactly 6 kilograms of the apples to be peeled and cooked into unsweetened applesauce because chewing whole apples is difficult for her. I wanted to make sure the group knows this before we decide on the split.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: I confirmed with the community pantry coordinator that they can accept exactly 12 kilograms of whole apples, packed as twelve labeled one-kilogram boxes, with delivery on Sunday at 10:00. So we have a concrete target for the donation side if we want to use it.
transcript.speaker: A3

transcript.text: I should mention something before we finalize the plan. I received a recommendation from the county extension food-preservation adviser that the remaining 12 kilograms should be made into unsweetened applesauce and frozen in twenty-four 500-gram containers rather than stored fresh. I haven't passed this on until now, but it seems especially relevant given Jonah's request for Grandma's applesauce and the freezer storage category we're planning.
